title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RB_1RE1LE_1LF0LA_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RB_1RE1LE_1LF0LA_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. The head sweeps over the whole tape, which is made of a handful of words in an order that keeps changing. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting configurations and no halt in the first 107 steps. The word structure below is observed in simulations, not proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,898 cells have been visited and 29,096 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.446). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.532).

claims.title: E never reads 0 with a 0 to its left (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is F reading a 0, and F is entered only from E>0 (write 1, move left): the machine halts exactly when 0 E>0 occurs. In the first 108 steps F is entered 6,990,496 times, always onto a 1.

claims.title: A tape of words
claims.text: Left of the start the tape is a sequence of the words 001010 (01)^3 1^6, (00101)^k 1^4, 0 1^7 and a few others; right of the start, words such as 1010 111 010110 (101)^3 (01101)^3 and (10110)^4 (11010)^3 1. Long stretches are periodic for a while (e.g. ((00101)^3 1^4 001010 (01)^3 1^6)^7 at step 9,863,880) and are then rewritten.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No regular macro structure has been found; the words are rewritten as the head passes and the sequence they form has no visible period. A proof would need the set of words to be closed under the head's passes (a closed-language argument) or a counter structure hidden in the word sequence.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine sweeps back and forth over a tape made of a few kinds of word, such as 001010 010101 111111 and 0 1111111, which it keeps rewriting and rearranging. No pattern in the arrangement has been found.

facts.text: No halt, checked by Lean's kernel (10<sup>7</sup> by compiled code).
No halt in the C simulator.
Entries into the halting state F in 10<sup>8</sup> steps, all onto a 1.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0 (E writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly when 0 E>0 occurs: E on a 0 with another 0 left of it. In the first 108 steps that happens 7 million times with a 1 to the left every time; the most common windows as F is entered are 110[1]110, 101[1]110, 011[1]111 and 101[1]111.

html: When the head reaches a new cell at the left end, the start of the tape looks like

The second sample has seven copies of (00101)^3 1^4 001010 (01)^3 1^6 in a row, but they do not last: the next sweeps rewrite the stretch into other words. The right side is built the same way from other words, such as 1010 111 010110 (101)^3 (01101)^3. Nothing here is proved; the run has not been reduced to rules.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.446). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.532).
After 109 steps the tape spans 48,898 cells (11,736 left of the start, 24,225 right), with a density of 1s of 0.595.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Bouncer whose tape is a sequence of a few dozen-cell words: on the left mainly 001010(01)^3 1^6, (00101)^3 1^4 and 0 1^7, on the right words built from 101, 01101 and 10110; the order of the words changes from sweep to sweep with no visible period. No regime proved.
family: bouncer over an irregular sequence of words
